result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_node_vitality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the vitality of a single node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L20304-L20408){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_node_vitality(node) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Node vitality measures the impact of removing a node on graph connectivity, defined as the change in sum of all pairwise shortest path distances: vitality(v) = sum_distances(G) - sum_distances(G - v) Higher values indicate more important nodes whose removal would significantly increase average path lengths or disconnect the graph. Infinite values indicate the node's removal disconnects the graph. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Node ID (int) or label (str) to compute vitality for. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The vitality score for the node. Higher values indicate more vital nodes. Returns `inf` if removing the node disconnects the graph. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the node does not exist in the graph. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Vitality is defined as the increase in the network's total pairwise distance caused by removing a single node: $\mathrm{vit}(v) = W(G) - W(G - v)$, where $W(G) = \sum_{u \ne w} d(u, w)$ is the Wiener index. Positive values flag nodes whose absence stretches out communication paths; $+\infty$ specifically flags cut vertices whose removal disconnects the graph and leaves some distances undefined. Because computing $W$ requires an all-pairs shortest-path pass, the cost is $O(V \cdot E)$ per node, so for many nodes it is dramatically cheaper to call `closeness_vitality()` once and read every value out of the same shared BFS pass. ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a path graph, removing a middle node splits the graph in two, which drives its vitality to infinity, while removing an endpoint barely changes anything: ::: {#d55ef316 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_path_graph(5) nodes = sorted(graph.get_node_ids()) # Removing a middle node disconnects the graph graph.get_node_vitality(nodes[2]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 36.0 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#318a995b .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Removing an endpoint has a small, finite effect graph.get_node_vitality(nodes[0]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 20.0 ``` ::: ::: The same pattern shows up in a star graph: the hub is critical to every path between leaves, while any individual leaf is comparatively unimportant: ::: {#b1d8fd8e .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_star_graph(4) nodes = sorted(graph.get_node_ids()) # Removing the hub disconnects all leaves from each other graph.get_node_vitality(nodes[0]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 18.0 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#fe7f82cc .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Removing a leaf barely changes total distances graph.get_node_vitality(nodes[1]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` 10.0 ``` ::: ::: Node labels work just as well as IDs: ::: {#7980ed81 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) # B connects A and C, so removing it disconnects the graph graph.get_node_vitality("B") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` 8.0 ``` ::: :::
